trial_court: Additional District Judge, Nagod, District Satna
case_name: Anokh Kumar @ Nukki Rajak Vs. Anjana Rajak and another.
facts_of_case: Appellant filed a Civil Suit under Section 12, 5(2) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for declaring the marriage solemnized in the year 2003 as null and void. The suit was decided ex-parte vide order dated 26.02.2015 and decree was passed in favour of the appellant declaring the marriage void.

legal_principles.principle: Burden lies on the party seeking to set aside an ex parte decree to prove that notice was not served.
legal_principles.held: The Court below has observed that in view of statements of the husband/appellant that he has admitted that village Itma is at the distance of about 3 to 4 kilometers from Devendra Nagar and Itma is a very rural area.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 9 Rule 13

legal_principles.principle: A party's intention to deceive or suppress information can be inferred from their conduct and admissions.
legal_principles.held: He has also admitted that he has filed the suit for seeking a decree of divorce suppressing this fact from the wife/respondent No.1 and he has also admitted that his intention was clear for not intimating this fact to his wife/respondent No.1.
use_in: cases involving intentional concealment of information

outcome.final_order: The application filed by the respondents under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was allowed.
